statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-21637 is a Node.js TLS denial of service: an exception thrown synchronously from an SNICallback bypasses the TLS error handlers and crashes the process. Node.js reused this id for an incomplete fix: its January 2026 release (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/december-2025-security-releases) wrapped the PSK and ALPN callbacks, and its March 2026 release says SNICallback was left unprotected in every release that carried that fix, 22.x included. Node.js fixed it for 22.x in 22.22.2, the 2026-03-24 security release (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/march-2026-security-releases), with commit 91b970886f, 'tls: wrap SNICallback invocation in try/catch' (https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/91b970886f), which carries this CVE id. Release notes: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v22.22.2. The CVE record's version list (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-21637) still describes only the January fix, through 22.21.1; we follow the March release, which covers 22.22.0 and 22.22.1 as well. We read the node binary in every published DHI nodejs-22 package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64: 22.22.2-r0 is the first that reports Node.js v22.22.2 and contains the try/catch around the SNICallback invocation that this commit adds; 22.22.0-r0 and 22.22.1-r0 report Node.js 22.22.0 and 22.22.1 and lack it. We also ran upstream's regression test for the fix (test/parallel/test-tls-psk-alpn-callback-exception-handling.js) against every published Alpine 3.23 aarch64 build: it does not complete and is killed after 180 seconds on 22.22.0-r0 and 22.22.1-r0, and passes on 22.22.2-r0 through 22.23.5-r0. Both earlier builds predate the fix, so the range starts at 0.

CVE-2026-21637 is a Node.js TLS denial of service: synchronous exceptions thrown by TLS server callbacks during the handshake bypass the TLS error handlers, crashing the process or leaking file descriptors. Node.js 24.13.0, the 2026-01-13 security release announced at https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/december-2025-security-releases, fixed the pskCallback and ALPNCallback paths with commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/20591b0618, which carries this CVE id. The SNICallback path was left unprotected, and the 2026-03-24 release reissued this CVE id as an incomplete fix. Node.js completed the fix for 24.x in 24.14.1, the 2026-03-24 security release, which lists 24.x among the affected lines: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/march-2026-security-releases. The completing fix is commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/df8fbfb93d, 'tls: wrap SNICallback invocation in try/catch', which carries this CVE id. The range ends at the first build that carries both parts of the fix, so builds with only the 24.13.0 part stay on the affected side. Release notes: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.14.1. We read the node binary in the DHI nodejs-24 packages for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64 from the first published build through the boundary, each checked against its index checksum: 24.13.0-r0, 24.13.1-r0 and 24.14.0-r0 report Node.js v24.13.0, v24.13.1 and v24.14.0, and 24.14.1-r0 is the first that reports Node.js v24.14.1. The try/catch around the SNICallback call that commit df8fbfb93d adds to the TLS code embedded in the node binary is present in 24.14.1-r0 and absent from the three earlier builds, on both architectures. The later packages in the DHI Alpine repository are versioned 24.15.0-r0 to 24.22.3-r0.
